 India set to be most resilient among 10 major economies in 2026-30: Assocham press trust of india New Delhi, 12 November India is projected to emerge as the most resilient economy among the world’s 10 leading economies during 2026-30, with a score of 71 out of 100, fol- lowed by China at 66, accord- ing to an Assocham report. Japan and Russia jointly ranked third with 60 points each, followed by Germany (59), Italy and Brazil (53 each), the UK (52), France (40) and the US (36), the report titled ‘India’s Economic Edge in the Top Ten Economies’ said. The assessment by the in- dustry lobby is based on 10 macroeconomic indicators, including real GDP growth, export growth, current ac- count balance, government debt, ﬁscal balances, real GDP per capita growth, gross na- tional savings and gross capi- tal formation. Using data from the International Monetary Fund’s World Economic Out- look database, the industry lobby ranked the 10 econ- omies on each indicator, with the best-performing country receiving the top rank. These rankings were converted into marks and aggregated to ar- rive at the overall score. The analysis covers 2021-25 as the retrospective period and 2026-30 as the forward- looking period, with 2025 and 2026 also assessed as individ- ual years. India secured the top position for 2026-30 on the back of its ﬁrst rank in real GDP growth and real GDP per capita growth.
